# Limits, open questions, and directions {#sec-limits}

**Every claim in this book has a boundary, and this chapter states each one
as a fact about the evidence: what was measured, on which split, with which
instrument, and what would move it.** The claims themselves live in the
evidence chapters with their numbers; here each is reduced to its limit, so
that a reader can tell a settled result from an open one at a glance, and
the chapter ends with the two outcomes that would change the
recommendation.

```{python}
#| label: setup-limits
#| include: false
import json, statistics
from pathlib import Path
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
from palette import *
RES = Path("..") / "results"
mean = statistics.mean
```

## What is established {#sec-established}

**Eleven results are settled to the standard of the fair-comparison protocol
(@sec-protocol); the last two rest on a single dataset and are labeled so.**
Each carries its numbers and its scope in its home section; this chapter
adds only the limits. Ratios are baseline ÷ ISLA, so above one favors ISLA.

| result | where |
|---|---|
| On HiLiftAeroML surface pressure, GeoTransolver and Transolver fed the unit freestream direction lead ISLA at every rung where it is measured: 35 and 210 random training cases, 4 and 21 training geometries, and the fixed angle. The deficit is not count noise: on the 35-case rung GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is 0.73 at the reporting protocol of 200,000 cells against 0.72 at the exploration budget, and at the fixed angle 0.69 against 0.68 while every model improves 20 to 25% from the one budget to the other. | @sec-data-efficiency, @sec-scoreboard-200k |
| On DrivAerML at the reporting protocol ISLA and GeoTransolver are at parity at full data (0.998) and ISLA leads Transolver by 6%; below full data GeoTransolver is the more data-efficient model, by a deficit that narrows from 17% at 27 cars to zero at 435 (0.83, 0.86, 0.92, 0.97, 1.00 at 27, 54, 109, 218, 435 cars, GeoTransolver at its better rate on every rung). | @sec-scoreboard-200k, @sec-full-data, @sec-deficit-anatomy |
| Rotation and translation covariance are exact by construction; with every case in a random pose ISLA scores 1.015x its native-frame error on DrivAerML and leads the rotation-augmented GeoTransolver and Transolver by 12% and 21% at the reporting protocol (@sec-nb-p200k-pose-verdict). | @sec-pose, @sec-isla-contracts |
| ISLA's prediction is consistent under a change of the inference draw: under a 10:1 front-to-back density bias with exact Horvitz–Thompson weights on DrivAerML at 100,000 cells (the labeled scaling budget) its error grows 1.07 to 1.2x where GeoTransolver's grows 8.7x and Transolver's 5.3x; under a stratified draw every model moves under 2%. Under refinement, ISLA converges across samplers, and so do GeoTransolver and Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + Horvitz–Thompson-centered datapipe (ablation); GeoTransolver and Transolver as released do not. | @sec-consistency-bench, @sec-scoreboard-consistency, @sec-nb-steelman-verdict |
| ISLA's trained function depends weakly on the training sampling law, on two datasets: trained under the area-proportional law and scored on the independent uniform draw, ISLA is 0.99x its uniform-trained twin on the 35-wing rung (200,000 cells) and 1.08x on the 435 cars (100,000 cells), GeoTransolver 2.6x and 7.9x, Transolver 2.4x and 9.6x. Weakly dependent, not indifferent: the cars' 8% exceeded the 5% clause preregistered for it. | @sec-training-law, @sec-sampling-laws |
| Training needs no rate sweep at the protocol rate 1e-3 at width 192, but under the default linear routing the safe rate has a ceiling that falls like 1/width and at least 1/depth: the rule rate 1e-3 × 192/width × 12/layers is the best clean rate at 384 and 768 wide and at 24 layers, and 48 layers has no clean linear rate. Above the ceiling the loss rises to the mean-field plateau, which is total routing collapse (every point routes to one slice in every block, anchors coincident). Cosine routing (bounded logits) removes the ceiling on every DrivAerML lane at neutral accuracy at the rule rates (cosine ÷ linear 0.998, 1.005, 1.020 at 192, 384, 768); its wing lanes are pending. The step cost is at parity with GeoTransolver at 10,000 tokens in half the memory. | @sec-robustness-lr, @sec-using-lr, @sec-isla-cost, @sec-nb-routingsat-verdict, @sec-nb-routenorm-cars-verdict |
| On the DrivAerML interior at 200,000 boundary cells and 200,000 queries ISLA leads GeoTransolver-volume on velocity (1.42), trails on pressure (0.87) and is level on eddy viscosity (0.98); single dataset, and ISLA's pressure seeds are 8% apart. | @sec-interior |
| Nothing tested generalizes across a flow-regime boundary. | @sec-regime-extrapolation |
| Cross-family transfer is a property of the training data for every architecture tested. | @sec-limits-transfer |
| *Single dataset (DrivAerML, 435 cars, 100,000 cells).* ISLA holds the accuracy-versus-memory frontier below about 70 GB: ISLA 384 wide at 100,000 cells scores 0.0411 at 22 GB against GeoTransolver 1,024 wide at 100,000 cells 0.0406 at 74 GB and GeoTransolver 512 wide at 200,000 cells 0.0410 at 100 GB. Cells stop paying above 100,000 for every model, and the 500-epoch protocol is converged. | @sec-equal-budget |
| *Single dataset (DrivAerML, 435 cars, 100,000 cells).* Both architectures reach the same capacity floor, about 0.040: ISLA with cosine routing reaches 0.0407 at 68M parameters (384 wide, 24 layers) and 0.0406 at 136M (48 layers); GeoTransolver reaches 0.0406 at 143M (1,024 wide) and 0.0403 at 571M (2,048 wide, estimated). At matched parameters near 140M the two are identical, and ISLA is within 1% of the floor at half GeoTransolver's parameters. | @sec-equal-budget |

## Limits of each headline claim {#sec-review-honesty}

### The HiLiftAeroML ladder: what its curves measure {#sec-limits-data-efficiency}

**GeoTransolver and Transolver fed the unit direction lie below ISLA at
both random-case rungs where ISLA is measured, at a ratio that narrows from
the smaller training set to the larger; the ladder is a statement about the
range of data every production CFD dataset in this program occupies, not a
scaling law.** The quantity throughout is the surface-pressure relative L2
of @sec-metrics averaged over the 180 validation cases shared by every
rung, in float32.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ladder-unit-drive
#| fig-cap: >
#|   The HiLiftAeroML ladder under the unit-direction protocol at the
#|   exploration budget (10,000 sampled cells per case). Surface pressure
#|   error on the shared 180-case validation set against the number of
#|   training cases, log-log, float32; marks are seed means and small dots
#|   the individual seeds. ISLA (filled blue squares), GeoTransolver (red
#|   circles) and Transolver (amber triangles, dashed) at the two rungs
#|   where all three are trained, 35 and 210 cases, each at its declared
#|   learning rate. How to read this: GeoTransolver and Transolver lie below
#|   ISLA at both rungs. The figure shows only the random-case rungs where all three
#|   architectures are trained; it does not show the 510- and 1,260-case
#|   rungs, the geometry and fixed-angle splits (@sec-scoreboard), or the
#|   reporting protocol of 200,000 cells (@sec-scoreboard-200k). Protocol:
#|   10,000 sampled cells per case, 500 epochs, bfloat16 training, no
#|   augmentation. Data: results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_2026-09-09.json,
#|   results/fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_35_2026-09-09.json,
#|   results/udrvl_210_reduction_2026-09-10.json,
#|   results/relframe_reduction_2026-09-11.json,
#|   results/frame_reduction_2026-09-11.json.
#| code-fold: true
J = lambda p: json.load(open(RES / p))
fpall = J("fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_2026-09-09.json")["runs"]; fp35 = J("fp32_reeval/fp32_shift_35_2026-09-09.json")["runs"]
u210 = J("udrvl_210_reduction_2026-09-10.json")
rf = J("relframe_reduction_2026-09-11.json")["hilift_val"]; ff = J("frame_reduction_2026-09-11.json")["hilift_val"]
p32 = lambda runs, names: [runs[n]["fields"]["pressure_l2"]["fp32_mean"] for n in names]
a210 = u210["three_seed_addendum_fp32"]
series = {
    "isla_ref": {35: [rf[f"rf_hl_mt2_meas_super_scarce_seed{s}"]["pressure_l2"] for s in (42, 43)],
                 210: [ff[f"rf_hl_mt2_meas_scarce_seed{s}"]["pressure_l2"] for s in (42, 43)]},
    "gt": {35: p32(fp35, [f"udrv_hl_gt_super_scarce_lr3e3_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43)]),
           210: a210["gt_unit_lr1e3"]["seed_pressure"]},
    "t": {35: p32(fp35, [f"udrv_hl_transolver_super_scarce_lr3e3_seed{s}" for s in (42, 43, 44)]),
          210: a210["transolver_unit_lr3e3"]["seed_pressure"]},
}
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.6, 4.9))
for key in ("isla_ref", "gt", "t"):
    d = series[key]; xs = sorted(d)
    ax.plot(xs, [mean(d[x]) for x in xs], **series_kwargs(key, zorder=3))
    for x in xs:
        ax.scatter([x] * len(d[x]), d[x], s=12, color=STYLE[key]["color"], zorder=4)
lines = ["baseline ÷ ISLA (seed means)"]
for x in (35, 210):
    ref = mean(series["isla_ref"][x])
    lines.append(f"{x:,} cases: GeoTransolver {mean(series['gt'][x])/ref:.2f}, Transolver {mean(series['t'][x])/ref:.2f}")
note(ax, "\n".join(lines), loc="lower left")
ax.legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8.5)
ax.set_xscale("log"); ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xticks([35, 210, 510, 1260]); ax.set_xticklabels(["35", "210", "510", "1,260"])
ax.set_yticks([0.04, 0.06, 0.1, 0.15]); ax.set_yticklabels(["0.04", "0.06", "0.10", "0.15"])
ax.yaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter()); ax.xaxis.set_minor_formatter(mpl.ticker.NullFormatter())
ax.set_xlim(25, 1800); ax.set_ylim(0.035, 0.2)
ax.set_xlabel("training cases [count]"); ax.set_ylabel("surface pressure error, area-weighted relative L2 [–]")
ax.set_title("HiLiftAeroML nested splits, unit-direction protocol, float32, exploration budget (10,000 cells)")
ax.grid(True, which="major"); ax.grid(False, which="minor")
fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

Three facts bound what the curves can say.

- **On the random-case ladder ISLA is measured at two rungs, 35 and 210
  cases.** Its ratio at 510 and 1,260 cases is not known; GeoTransolver's
  and Transolver's curves continue to those rungs (@sec-scoreboard), and the expectation
  from the recurrence reading below is a ratio somewhat lower than at 210
  cases. The geometry and fixed-angle splits are separate ladders with
  their own rungs (@sec-scoreboard).
- **Every seed at a rung trains on the same curated subset**, so the seed
  bands measure initialization, not the choice of training cases.
  Geometry-stratified redraws of the 35- and 210-case training sets put the
  GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA ratio inside a band that stays below one on every
  draw (@sec-scoreboard), so the curated draws are typical.
- **The wing deficit does not move with the cell count.** On the 35-case
  rung GeoTransolver ÷ ISLA is 0.73 at 200,000 cells against 0.72 at
  10,000, and at the fixed angle 0.69 against 0.68 while every model
  improves 20 to 25% between the two budgets (@sec-scoreboard-200k); the
  deficit is a property of the trained functions, not of the sampling.

### The HiLift accuracy figures are validation-set figures {#sec-limits-validation}

**Every HiLiftAeroML accuracy number in this book is scored on the shared
180-case validation set on final-epoch checkpoints; no checkpoint is
selected on validation error, but no HiLiftAeroML split remains that could
confirm the numbers independently of the program's own history.** The
validation set entered more than one decision: each architecture's
learning-rate choice on the full split (@sec-lr-protocol), Transolver's
rate per small-data rung, the design of the ablations, and the choice of
what to present. The sealed test splits were spent on regime extrapolation
and the deflection split, which train on different cases but between them
read every one of the 180 geometries, and their manifests overlap the
data-efficiency test set on most of its cases
(results/hilift_exposure_ledger_2026-09-08.json). Every remaining test
split is therefore *held out per checkpoint*, since no model trained on
it, but not a *program-level confirmation*, and removing already-read cases
after the fact would define a selected population, not a replacement. A
sealed evaluation of the 35-case checkpoints on the 360 test cases would be
a within-protocol held-out check of the 35-case ratios and is not yet
measured (@sec-program-status); an independent confirmation needs
geometries no part of the program has scored, which on HiLiftAeroML means a
prospective dataset.

### Mechanism: what is known and what is not {#sec-limits-mechanism}

**The in-distribution gap is decomposed, and the parts that remain
unexplained are small; what is not known is whether any of them can be
removed without breaking a contract.** The decomposition itself is
@sec-deficit-anatomy; the limits on it are these.

- **No single ingredient of ISLA is load-bearing for its own accuracy.**
  Five single-factor ablations at 35 wing cases each move the error by
  between −12% and +16% (@sec-mechanism). The exactness of the covariance
  contract neither costs nor buys anything measurable in distribution at
  that rung; at 435 cars and the exploration budget the positional
  information the contracts deny is worth about two and a half points of
  the ratio, measured by a diagnostic that breaks the contract and is not a
  configuration (@sec-deficit-anatomy).
- **The wing deficit is representational, not a shortage of training
  cases.** With the data axis removed (one case, 64 resampled views,
  trained to convergence: the error reached this way is the model's
  *one-case floor*, a measurement of capacity rather than of
  generalization), ISLA's floor is above both baselines' by more than the
  35-case gap; the deficit sits on the smooth, large-cell regions that
  dominate the area-weighted metric, not at the gaps between wing elements
  (@sec-nb-overfit-verdict). On the cars there is no deficit left to
  explain: at the reporting protocol the two architectures are at parity at
  full data, share most of their residual on identical points
  (@sec-shared-floor), and reach the same capacity floor of about 0.040 as
  width and depth grow (@sec-equal-budget, single dataset). Which part of
  the wing representation carries the deficit is partly known and partly
  refuted: on the one-case instrument eight independent routings per block
  remove most of the form gap, but on the full DrivAerML training set eight
  routings are null, so the one-case ordering does not transfer and
  routing multiplicity is not the carrier (@sec-nb-heads435-verdict).
- **The origin-free frame's price on the wings is mesher pattern.** Against
  the legacy centered variant (removed; a plain-mean center with a fixed
  length unit) ISLA pays nothing on DrivAerML and on the
  never-seen-geometry rungs, and about a tenth where validation geometries
  recur in training. Two diagnostics with an exact full-geometry frame pay
  more than ISLA, so the price is not positional information but the
  mesh-density content of the plain-mean center, which is reusable when a
  wing returns and a liability when it does not
  (@sec-nb-frame-full-verdict). The fixed angle is the one
  never-seen-geometry rung where ISLA still pays; the reading that a single
  freestream direction makes the mesher's refinement pattern a geometric
  cue that transfers within the wing family is consistent with every rung
  and not separately tested.
- **The measure weights' price is variance plus mesh pattern, and only the
  variance part shrinks.** On the cars the weights-off ÷ weights-on ratio
  rises toward one with cell count; on the wings it is flat across a
  sixteen-fold range, which variance cannot produce, and the weights-off
  checkpoints lose consistency under an area-proportional draw, with errors
  worse than predicting zero (@sec-consistency-bench). Weights off is an
  ablation that prices the measure semantics, never a configuration
  (@sec-principle).
- **The interior standings sort into capacity and generalization** on the
  single-car instrument: the velocity lead is capacity, and the pressure
  standing reverses with the data fixed, so what pressure lead ISLA has at
  full data is generalization across cars (@sec-interior-open).
- **The contracts are exact in float32 and not in bf16.** On the trained
  GPU path the rotation and translation residual is 3e-5 at worst in
  float32 and 4% (pressure) to 7% (wall shear) under the bf16 autocast the
  recipe trains with, mostly ordinary rounding (2.3% with no motion at all).
  A bf16 deployment does not exercise the contracts at the level the book
  claims for them; float32 inference does (@sec-isla-contracts,
  @sec-using-sampler).

### Regime extrapolation fails for every architecture tested {#sec-limits-regime}

**Neither architecture generalizes across a flow-regime boundary, and
ISLA's structure does not change that.** The readout is the out-of-regime
sealed-test pressure error divided by the in-regime validation error.
Trained at angles of attack up to 12° and tested at 14° and above, or
trained pre-stall and tested post-stall, both architectures lose about a
factor of ten, and the out-of-regime errors are worse than either reaches
from 35 in-regime cases (@sec-regime-extrapolation). Both GeoTransolver
regime runs consumed the physical velocity, so the ratios there are
physical-velocity measurements; ISLA keeps the lower absolute error on both
sides of the boundary. Whether GeoTransolver's smaller degradation ratio
comes from its raw-coordinate inputs was tested directly with a
raw-coordinate channel on ISLA (which breaks the covariance contract); the
preregistered falsifier fired, so the smaller ratio is not carried by raw
coordinates and no mechanism for it has been isolated
(@sec-ood-mechanism). Coverage of the regime, not architecture, governs
this axis. Along one geometry parameter of one wing family the picture is
the same: on the deflection split, trained on the milder 80% of geometries
and tested once on the most aggressive 20%, both architectures degrade by
the same factor and the in-regime ordering carries through
(@sec-nb-deflection-verdict). A split across geometry *classes* remains the
open test, and none of this book's datasets provides one.

### Interior accuracy {#sec-limits-interior}

**The interior standing at the reporting protocol, a velocity lead (1.42),
a pressure deficit (0.87) and level eddy viscosity (0.98) against
GeoTransolver-volume, holds at the training query count on one dataset,
and its pressure part is inside ISLA's own seed spread.** Six limits bound
it (@sec-interior). The comparison is not resource-matched and the two
models do not receive the same inputs, and GeoTransolver-volume fed the
physical velocity changes by under 2% on every field, so the ratios are not
an input-scale artifact. ISLA's two pressure seeds are 8% apart, so the
pressure ratio is the least settled of the three. The full-data standings
only partly extend to small data: at 54 and 109 training cars the velocity
lead is smaller (@tbl-interior-smalldata). The interacting decode's
prediction depends on the joint query set, training over a range of counts
reduces the dependence without removing it, and the passive decode's
dependence is exactly zero, so the interacting configuration is deployed at
its training count (@sec-interior-companion). The interior evidence lanes
were trained under the older `geometric_mean` query-mass option, not the
default `source_total`, so the standing under the default is not yet
measured. And the eddy-viscosity metric is on a standardized field, so its
ratios are orderings under that centering, not physical percentages. The
far-wake eddy-viscosity gap that dominated the interior picture at the
exploration budget, and that the single-car test identified as capacity
(@sec-interior-open), closes to 2% at the reporting protocol; what remains
open is pressure.

### Exact query independence costs about three times in accuracy {#sec-limits-query-independence}

**ISLA's surface predictions depend weakly on which other points are
sampled; making them exactly independent costs 3.0 to 3.7x in surface
accuracy, so every surface checkpoint behind the headline results is the
interacting configuration** (@sec-query-independence). Swapping the
companion set moves a surface point's prediction by about 7%
(GeoTransolver's by about 2% at a shared prefix). The passive decoder is
exactly independent in float64 and 3.0 to 3.7x less accurate on DrivAerML
surface pressure, and the interior confirms the price at matched depth and
inputs: a twelve-block passive decode from an interacting support set
carrying the signed distance still costs 1.43x on pressure and 2.41x on
eddy viscosity against the interacting query tokens
(@sec-interior-query-independence). What the interacting queries provide is
computation at the requested points through every encoder layer, not
geometric context. Evaluate-anywhere semantics is a contract with a measured
price, and ISLA does not carry it.

### Cross-family transfer is a data property {#sec-limits-transfer}

**Neither ISLA nor GeoTransolver transfers zero-shot across vehicle
families; what moves cross-family error is the diversity of the training
data, and ISLA pays more than GeoTransolver for both halving its source
data and mixing in a sibling family** (@tbl-frontier in @sec-full-data).
On the held-out fastback family the models trained on DrivAerML alone score
close to the mean predictor, ISLA's failure worse than GeoTransolver's, and
a second training family moves both to a usable error. Few-shot adaptation
separates them further: fine-tuned on 20 fastback cases, GeoTransolver's
head start over training from scratch grows while ISLA's shrinks, so what
GeoTransolver learns on DrivAerML is the better starting point for a new
family (research/transfer_program/studies/campaign_c_transfer). No single
ISLA ingredient carries that deficit: retraining with more or fewer
anchors, raw seeds, the similarity-gauge variant (removed) or the weights
off moves the zero-shot error nowhere near GeoTransolver's
(@sec-nb-xfam-verdict), so the cross-family question is a data question.
Diversity at a fixed label budget is a trade: splitting 435 training cases
between DrivAerML and a sibling family buys the target family almost
entirely and costs the source about what halving its data costs, plus a few
percent for the mixing, and the mixing cost grows with the foreign share
for ISLA and not for GeoTransolver; a per-case family flag changes nothing,
so the mismatch is coverage, not identification. A claim of family-portable
surface physics from any of these architectures would need a corpus in
which geometry, pose, scale and regime vary one at a time.

## Open questions, and what would settle each {#sec-open-questions}

**Each open question carries a readout and, where one has been written, a
preregistered bar; the live status of every item is in @sec-program-status
and the preregistrations are in the notebook.** Unless stated, the readout
is the surface-pressure relative L2 of @sec-metrics and the ratio is
baseline ÷ ISLA, so above one favors ISLA.

| question | what would settle it | bar |
|---|---|---|
| What is the mechanism of the wing deficit? | the mesher-pattern hypothesis (validation geometries recur in training with a different mesh) tested by a split that holds geometries out entirely at matched case count, at the reporting protocol | the ratio moves toward parity when recurrence is removed, or does not |
| What is ISLA's ratio on the two largest HiLift rungs? | ISLA trained at 510 and 1,260 cases at the reporting protocol | reported as measured; the prediction from the recurrence reading is a ratio somewhat below the 210-case value |
| Do the 35-case ratios hold on cases no decision has read? | the 35-case ISLA and unit-direction baseline checkpoints scored once on the 360-case sealed test | the validation ratios reproduced within their seed spread |
| Does bounding the routing logits remove the linear-routing rate ceiling on a second dataset? | cosine routing at the rates that collapse linear routing on the 510-wing rung, and the reporting-protocol lanes on the 35-wing rung and on the cars (@sec-nb-routenorm-prereg, @sec-nb-routenorm-p200k-prereg) | answered on DrivAerML (clean training at every collapse rate, neutral accuracy at the rule rates; @sec-nb-routenorm-cars-verdict); pending on the 510-wing rung, and the cosine default waits on it |
| Why does ISLA's training-law dependence differ between datasets (1% on the wings, 8% on the cars)? | the twin training under a third law, or on a third dataset, with the same independent uniform readout (@sec-training-law) | no bar is preregistered; reported as measured |
| Does the architecture match a same-size baseline on a problem that is not external aerodynamics? | a dataset outside external aerodynamics with GeoTransolver trained on it under the fair-comparison protocol; the screened-Poisson acceptance case already trains with $K = 0$ global vectors and one global scalar (@sec-nb-globin-accept-verdict) | the error at the level of the same-size baseline on that problem |
| Does either architecture extrapolate across geometry classes? | a split across classes rather than along one parameter of one family | none of this book's datasets provides one |
| Is the interior pressure deficit real or seed noise? | third seeds of the interior configuration at the reporting protocol under the default query-mass convention and, if adopted, cosine routing; the current pair reads 0.87 with ISLA's seeds 8% apart | no bar is preregistered; the velocity lead and level eddy viscosity must not move by more than 5% |

## Engineering directions {#sec-future}

**Five directions are engineering, not research: each has a measured
starting point and a stated remainder.**

| direction | what is in place | what remains |
|---|---|---|
| Problems outside external aerodynamics | the interface accepts zero or more global vector inputs and zero or more global scalar inputs, and per-cell boundary data through the boundary-scalar channel (@sec-isla-inputs); the contract tests cover zero and two global directions; a screened-Poisson acceptance case trains with no global vector and one global scalar, and the scalar is decisive where the boundary data cannot substitute for it (@sec-nb-globin-accept-verdict) | no production dataset outside external aerodynamics has a baseline trained on it under the protocol, and nothing in this book's measurements depends on one |
| Cost at scale | parity with GeoTransolver's step at 10,000 tokens in half the memory on the compiled path; the exact fused geometry kernel, the default on CUDA, holds the accuracy-versus-memory frontier below about 70 GB at 435 cars (@sec-isla-cost, @sec-equal-budget) | the fused kernel is single-routing only; the gap below GeoTransolver's footprint is headroom for more tokens or a wider model, though on DrivAerML neither buys accuracy past 100,000 cells and 384 wide under either routing |
| The in-distribution price of the measure weights | its mechanism is estimator variance in the slice states, removable by more cells or by the stratified inference draw (@sec-using-sampler) | a variance-reduced consistent quadrature at a fixed cell budget beyond stratification; the weights themselves are not the target (@sec-principle) |
| Sampling conventions | ISLA's convention-swap penalty converges under refinement, and so does that of GeoTransolver and Transolver + ISLA's measure-weighted pooling + Horvitz–Thompson-centered datapipe (ablation); GeoTransolver's and Transolver's as released does not (@sec-consistency-bench, @sec-nb-steelman-verdict) | at 10,000 cells no architecture is consistent across conventions; the fine-mesh limit is within a few percent of reached at 40,000 |
| Query-count consistency of the interior decode | `query_mass="source_total"` is the default: the total query mass is a learned fraction of the total source measure divided by the query count, so neither refining the source nor changing the request size moves the balance between surface and queries, and the passive readout is invariant to a rescaling of the measure (the defect it removes is stated in @sec-isla-contracts; @sec-nb-no-legacy-compat); count augmentation reduces the interacting decode's dependence by about 40% at a small cost | the interior evidence lanes were trained under the older `geometric_mean` option, so the interior standing under the default is not yet measured |

## What would change the recommendation {#sec-review-roads}

**On DrivAerML surface pressure at the reporting protocol ISLA and
GeoTransolver are at parity at full data and ISLA leads Transolver by 6%;
GeoTransolver leads below full data on the cars, by 17% at 27 cars
narrowing to zero at 435, and by 27% on the 35-wing rung; ISLA is the
choice wherever the deployment sampling may differ from the training
sampling, wherever the training sampling law is not the deployment one,
where geometries arrive in arbitrary poses, and where memory at scale
binds.** The recommendation splits on consistency, and consistency is a
property of the frame, not of the architecture: every configuration that
centers its coordinates on a statistic of the sampled points degrades
several-fold under a sampling-density bias when the frame is taken from the
biased sample, GeoTransolver and Transolver included, and only frames that
do not read the sample hold, ISLA's origin-free frame among them and the
ablations of GeoTransolver and Transolver given a Horvitz–Thompson center
(@sec-scoreboard-consistency, @sec-nb-steelman-verdict). Those ablations
locate the property; GeoTransolver and Transolver are stable, in use and
published, and are not modified, so measure weighting and a sample-free
frame reach users through ISLA (@sec-nb-ruling-released-baselines). Two
outcomes would change the recommendation.

**ISLA gains an in-distribution accuracy claim below full data and on the
wings** if the mechanism of the wing deficit is located and removed by a
principled configuration: the geometry-holdout test of @sec-open-questions
is the one such candidate, and the cosine routing decision, if it carries
the wing lanes, changes the training rule but not, on the DrivAerML
evidence, the accuracy at width 192. If the wing deficit closes, the
scoreboard gains rows in which GeoTransolver no longer leads at small data,
and the recommendation on matched-mesher, known-pose surface prediction
from few training cases becomes a trade of a few percent of accuracy
against the contracts rather than a preference for GeoTransolver.

**The interior recommendation becomes unconditional for ISLA** only if the
pressure deficit closes at width 192 without moving velocity or eddy
viscosity. The eddy-viscosity gap that the exploration budget located in
the far wake and the single-car test identified as capacity
(@sec-interior-open) closes to 2% at the reporting protocol; pressure
remains at 0.87 with ISLA's seeds 8% apart, so at the reporting protocol
the recommendation is ISLA on velocity, GeoTransolver-volume on pressure,
and either on eddy viscosity, on one dataset.

If neither fires, the recommendation stands as written, with the bounds of
this chapter attached: the program's ISLA-specific claims are exact
covariance and its lead in arbitrary poses, consistency under a change of
inference draw and weak dependence on the training sampling law as
properties of the origin-free frame and the measure weights, the passive
query-independent decode at its measured price, the interior velocity lead,
the cost figures of @sec-isla-cost, and on in-distribution surface accuracy
parity with GeoTransolver at full data on the cars, with a deficit below
full data and on the wings.
